We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

As we found previously, the slope is $m=-2.$

Substituting $m=-2$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=-2x+b.
$$

We now need to find the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can find this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(4,-3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-2x+b \\ -3 & =-2(4)+b \\ -3 & =-8+b \\ 5 & =b \\ b & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=-2x+5.
$$

We begin by moving all of the variables to the left-hand side and all of the constants to the right-hand side:

$$

Now, $a,b,$ and $c$ are integers with no common factors, and $a\ge 0.$ So, we are done!

The standard form of the line is 

$$

questions.worked_solution:
Perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other. Therefore, since $\overset{↔}{AB}$ has the slope $m=-2,$ our perpendicular line must have a slope of 

$$
{m}_{1}=-\frac{1}{m}=-\frac{1}{(-2)}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

So, our perpendicular line has the slope ${m}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}$ and passes through the point $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(10,3).$ 

Finally, using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & ={m}_{1}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-3 & =\frac{1}{2}(x-10) \\ y-3 & =\frac{1}{2}x-5 \\ y & =\frac{1}{2}x-2\end{aligned}
$$
